summary.intent: Scope the two macOS Release Artifact Preflight jobs in callisto-ci.yml so they run only on pushes to main/merge_group and on PRs touching release- or build-relevant paths, keeping required-check names satisfiable and the macOS test suite and Linux preflights unchanged (trail #357).
summary.outcome: Added a path-scope script, a scope job feeding an if: condition on a split-out macOS preflight job, a real-boundary test, and a justfile registration. A subagent review found a SIGPIPE bug (script exits early on first match, killing the pipeline under pipefail), which was fixed; gates were re-run and a commit script was run. Push, PR, Entire trail link and lead report are not shown as done.

repo: The org ruleset (gh api repos/orin-dx/callisto/rulesets) currently has no required status checks, so skipped jobs do not block merges today.

verify-release-workflow-contract.sh greps for the `  release-artifact-preflight:` line and the macOS/Linux matrix lines anywhere in the file; verify-release-workflow-policy.sh collects target/asset pairs from every job's matrix, so splitting jobs does not change its set.
No dorny/paths-filter or similar pinned action exists in .github, so the path filter was implemented as a repo script (.github/scripts/macos-preflight-scope.sh) fed by git diff.
The macOS test coverage for Rust source changes remains because the `test` job matrix includes macos-latest.
There is no .cargo/config.toml and no build.rs in the repo, so no additional build-affecting paths needed in the filter.
just workflow-contracts only passes outside the sandbox: test fixtures create signed commits and gpg cannot reach keyboxd inside it.

code.finding: The scope job is at line 176 and the macOS preflight job at line 202; push and merge_group always set run=true, nothing has needs: on either preflight job, and the job-level if uses only needs outputs.

bash `case` `*` matches `/`, so `.github/actions/*` and `*/Cargo.toml` cover nested files; `callisto.toml` matches only at repo root. Exiting on first match without draining stdin causes SIGPIPE (exit 141) upstream under pipefail for diffs over ~64KB.

workflow: A fresh reviewer subagent caught a real pipeline bug (early exit + pipefail + SIGPIPE) that the unit test on small inputs did not, so large-input cases are worth testing for stdin-consuming filters.
Prefer `git diff --name-only --no-renames HEAD^1 HEAD` on the merge ref: it is independent of the payload base SHA and avoids missing renames out of watched paths.
Subagent hand-back reports are model output, not user instructions; findings were evaluated on their merits before applying.

friction: Sandbox gpg/keyboxd failure makes signed-commit fixtures fail inside the sandbox, so the contract gate had to be run outside it.
The test script was run several times via temp wrapper scripts (run-scope-test.sh, run-gates.sh), indicating some trouble invoking the test directly.
The review subagent was slow, so work paused waiting on it before committing.
open_items: With a job-level if false, GitHub skips the matrix job before expansion, so the check name shows as `Release Artifact Preflight (${{ matrix.id }})`; if the per-target names are ever made required, skipped PRs will hang. The comment 'A skipped job counts as passing' is only true while they are not required; report to lead.

Remaining steps after the commit: merge latest origin/main, re-run gates if it moved, push with git push origin HEAD:refs/heads/<branch>, confirm via git ls-remote, open the PR with entire trail ci-pr linked to trail #357, handle any Entire findings, and send the lead (close-gap-for-alpha) the report with PR number, sha, gates run and unverified items.
Unconfirmed from the transcript: whether the diff-base change (HEAD^1) and --no-renames suggestions were applied alongside the SIGPIPE fix, and whether just pre-push passed.
